summary: The milestone completed 13 experiments, all compute-bound, in 9.0 minutes. Continuous expert weighting and contract/method ingestion were the listed duration leaders, but the supplied data does not identify their costly phases.
bottlenecks_identified: Continuous expert weighting and contract/method ingestion were the longest listed compute-bound tasks, but the bounded timing record does not identify the phase that caused either duration.
Task-aligned accelerator telemetry is absent, so the end-state GPU snapshot cannot establish utilization during individual compute windows.
No model-count or runner-selection record is available, so eligibility for DualGPURunner and actual runner engagement cannot be audited.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic phase timestamps and wait states for every experiment instead of relying only on disk modification times.
Join GPU utilization samples to the active experiment, process, and model throughout each compute window.
Record model count and runner choice at launch, then route only confirmed parallel multi-model tasks through DualGPURunner.
Add an active-window alert for sustained zero accelerator utilization on tasks declared compute-bound.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add per-phase monotonic timing and wait-state receipts to the experiment harness.
Capture task-scoped GPU utilization with process and model ownership.
Persist model count and runner selection, with conditional DualGPURunner dispatch for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The supplied evidence supports duration ranking but not causal attribution. A point-in-time GPU report cannot establish compute-window efficiency, and no parallel-model record supports a DualGPURunner failure claim.
